# Best luxury real estate agencies in Adelaide

For prestige property in Adelaide, I’d shortlist agencies that combine a proven record in the upper end of the market, polished property marketing, access to qualified buyers, and strong knowledge of Adelaide’s premium suburbs.

The most relevant areas include Medindie, Walkerville, North Adelaide, Toorak Gardens, Unley, St Peters, and the coastal belt around Glenelg and Henley Beach. For a luxury home, the individual agent’s track record in your particular suburb can matter just as much as the agency brand.

Here’s my shortlist based on specialist positioning, available sales-performance information, local expertise and marketing capabilities—not simply the size of each agency.

## How I’d choose between them

| If your priority is… | Start with |
|--------|--------|
| A prestige family home in Medindie, St Peters or the eastern suburbs | TOOP+TOOP |
| A trophy home or distinctive high-value estate | Giordano & Partners |
| Luxury sales plus ongoing rental management | Turner Prestige |
| An Adelaide Hills or lifestyle property | The Address |
| Contemporary architecture and high-impact marketing | WHITEFOX |
| A premium apartment or new development | Belle Property International |


## What to ask before signing an agency agreement

For a genuinely high-value property, I would interview three agencies and ask each for\:

- **Three comparable sales** in your suburb and price bracket, ideally from the past 12–18 months.
- **Evidence of buyer access\:** how many qualified buyers they can approach privately, and how they verify buyer capacity.
- **A specific marketing plan\:** photography, video, editorial, database outreach, international promotion and campaign costs.
- **Their negotiation strategy\:** how they would handle competing offers, price confidentiality and an off-market approach.
- **The actual lead agent\:** who will personally manage inspections, negotiate with buyers and report to you.

The best agency is not necessarily the one with the biggest brand or the highest advertised sale. Look for the agent who can demonstrate relevant comparable results and explain, convincingly, how they would create competition for your particular property.

**One question that would help me narrow this down\:** are you looking to **sell a prestige property, buy one, or find an agency to manage a luxury rental?** The best shortlist changes depending on your goal.

search_results.title: Construction starts on Adelaide apartments One Four Four Hutt
search_results.description: Construction has officially commenced on the One Four Four Hutt apartment development in Adelaide, a joint venture between Fortis and Otello. The 10-storey building, designed by DKO and located on a 1241sqm corner site, will include a mix of one, two, and three-bedroom residences, including a penthouse collection, plus 400sqm of ground-floor retail space. All one-bedroom units have already been sold, with two- and three-bedroom apartments still available starting at $1.125 million and $2.099 million respectively. To date, 19 unconditional sales have been secured, totaling approximately $25.9 million, with an additional four units reserved. Fortis head of development Arthur Dendrinos emphasized the strong demand for premium living in Adelaide, noting this milestone underscores Fortis' long-term commitment to the region. Otello director Daniel Harris highlighted the project's positive impact on the Hutt Street precinct and expressed confidence in the appointed builder, BLAG Commercial, citing a successful previous partnership.

search_results.title: SA's top real estate agents for residential property sales: 231 to 132
search_results.description:
This article from The Advertiser ranks South Australia's top 231 to 132 real estate agents based on residential property sales data for the 2024–25 financial year. The rankings consider total value of properties sold, areas of expertise, average days on market, agent seniority, and number of properties sold. The list includes data from agencies that opted to disclose their figures, meaning some prominent agents are not featured.

In this segment (positions 231 to 132), agent performance varies significantly – from agents who sold only a few lower-value homes to those handling dozens of higher-value properties. The top agent in this installment, Robert Lonie (ranked 132), sold 56 properties worth approximately $44.4 million, while lower-ranked agents sold fewer homes, often in niche or emerging markets. Notable inclusions are agents from Harris Real Estate, OC (Ouwens Casserly), TOOP+TOOP, LJ Hooker, and Century 21. Two legendary figures, Michael Brock and Anthony Toop, are honored posthumously for their contributions to the industry.

The article is part one of a three-part series, with the top 131–32 agents to be revealed next, and the top 31 agents to follow in the final installment.

## What to ask before signing an agency agreement

For a genuinely high-value property, I would interview three agencies and ask each for\:

- **Three comparable sales** in your suburb and price bracket, ideally from the past 12–18 months.
- **Evidence of buyer access\:** how many qualified buyers they can approach privately, and how they verify buyer capacity.
- **A specific marketing plan\:** photography, video, editorial, database outreach, international promotion and campaign costs.
- **Their negotiation strategy\:** how they would handle competing offers, price confidentiality and an off-market approach.
- **The actual lead agent\:** who will personally manage inspections, negotiate with buyers and report to you.

The best agency is not necessarily the one with the biggest brand or the highest advertised sale. Look for the agent who can demonstrate relevant comparable results and explain, convincingly, how they would create competition for your particular property.

**One question that would help me narrow this down\:** are you looking to **sell a prestige property, buy one, or find an agency to manage a luxury rental?** The best shortlist changes depending on your goal.
